elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph gives Customer only a licence ("Kubient grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense... all deliverables"); no ownership vests in Customer, and retained warranty (viii) still states Kubient is "the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the insertion is a licence grant only.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform", and warranty (viii) confirms Kubient's ownership of the Service and Auction Platform; nothing divests Vendor's own IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "a perpetual... license to use, modify and sublicense... all deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder other than the Auction Platform" — a deliverables licence necessarily reaches Vendor IP embedded in those deliverables (Auction Platform itself carved out and licensed separately under paragraph 2).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The grant is expressly "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Kubient's licence scope; there is no affirmative statement that Customer retains all right, title and interest in its Content, Requests and other data. Retained paragraph 25(a) allocates responsibility/liability for Content but not ownership of data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests, and any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing the same solely to provide the Services" — catch-all covers every category of Customer data.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No no-joint-ownership statement was added; the insertion is silent on joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Kubient grants Customer a perpetual... license" to deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"; the revocability in paragraph 2 attaches only to the separately carved-out Auction Platform licence, so there is no internal inconsistency.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense, for Customer's business, all deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder other than the Auction Platform"; paragraph 25(a)'s no-modification restriction is directed at "the Service"/"software included in any Service", which warranty (i) treats as distinct from "deliverables provided hereunder".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense, for Customer's business" in the inserted grant; paragraph 2's "without right of sublicense" applies only to the Auction Platform, which the new grant expressly excludes.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests, and any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing the same solely to provide the Services" — no distribution, resale or wider "purposes contemplated" carve-out remains.

reasons: The finding of 'missing' is sound: the Agreement has no IP/data-ownership article, and the only grant to Customer (paragraph 2) is limited, non-sublicensable and revocable, which fails the fallback on material terms.

Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted paragraph delivers Vendor retention of generic tools/know-how, and a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business, plus a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on any Kubient licence in Customer data.

Preferred is not complete: there is no Customer ownership of or assignment of Deliverables, no affirmative 'Customer retains all rights in Customer Data' sentence, and no express bar on joint ownership. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add (i) 'Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the deliverables and work product created for Customer', (ii) 'Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data', and (iii) 'No intellectual property will be jointly owned.'

Minimal: the insertion is a concise new paragraph for a missing clause, deletes nothing, adds no survival tail, expense or procedural boilerplate, and the 'other than the Auction Platform' carve-out is necessary to avoid contradicting the retained paragraph 2 licence rather than an extra. The words 'and the Auction Platform' in the retention sentence lightly overlap with warranty (viii) but serve as the anchor for that carve-out.

Preserves intent: paragraph 2's Auction Platform licence, paragraph 25(a)'s use restrictions on the Service, and the Kubient warranties survive without contradiction, and no new assignment exception or Vendor-favourable transfer right is created.

Drafting caution to verify before sending: confirm 'Requests' is a defined term in the Agreement; if it is not, drop the capitalisation or delete it, since the catch-all 'any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer' already carries the element and an undefined capitalised term risks a dangling reference.
